#import re #if $input_files.single_or_collection.input_single_or_collection == "single" #set $input_name = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($input_files.single_or_collection.query.element_identifier)) #set $input_ext = $input_files.single_or_collection.query.ext
#if $input_ext.endswith('.gz') #set $local_input_file = $input_name + '.gz' #elif $input_ext.endswith('.bz2') #set $local_input_file = $input_name + '.bz2' #else #set $local_input_file = $input_name #end if
#if 'bam' in $input_ext #set $format = 'bam' #elif 'sam' in $input_ext #set $format = 'sam' #else #set $format = 'fastq' #end if
ln -s '$input_files.single_or_collection.query' '$local_input_file' && #elif $input_files.single_or_collection.input_single_or_collection == "collection" ## FastQC reports on one file, so join the collection into one file ## named after the collection. #set $local_input_file = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($input_files.single_or_collection.query.name)) #set $format = 'fastq'
cat #for $file in $input_files.single_or_collection.query '$file' #end for > '$local_input_file' && #end if
mkdir -p fastqc-output && fastqc --outdir fastqc-output --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} --dir \${TEMP:-\$_GALAXY_JOB_TMP_DIR} --quiet --extract -f $format '$local_input_file' && cp fastqc-output/*/fastqc_data.txt '$text_file' && cp fastqc-output/*.html '$html_file'

param.name: query

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark See FastQC documentation: https://github.com/s-andrews/FastQC/blob/master/README.md for full software details.
**What it does** Runs quality control checks on raw sequence data. The HTML report has summary graphs and tables. The data file has the raw results.
A single file can be FASTQ (optionally gzip or bzip2 compressed), SAM or BAM. For a list collection of FASTQ files, the tool joins all reads into one file first and makes one combined report. To get one report for every file instead, select the files one by one in batch mode.
